sections.skill: Recognize when a document may be misread or incomplete

questions.domain: Everyday: searching and working with documents
questions.prompt: Which document is most likely to be misread by a tool?

choices.text: A clean typed page with plain, simple text
A blurry, tilted phone photo of a receipt

questions.correct_answer: A blurry, tilted phone photo of a receipt
questions.intro: Tools read documents less reliably when the documents are POOR QUALITY: blurry or tilted scans, handwriting, faint photocopies, complex tables, charts, or files where text is actually an image. They also struggle when documents are INCOMPLETE: missing pages, a cut-off photo, or a file that did not fully upload. The answer may still sound confident. Warning signs: numbers that do not add up, garbled words, answers that ignore a section you know exists. Fixes: upload a clearer copy, split complex tables, type key numbers yourself, and check that every page is present.

sections.skill: Spot signs of a misread document

questions.domain: Everyday: searching and working with documents
questions.prompt: Items 12 + 8 + 5, stated total 30. Which sign appears?

choices.text: Garbled words in the item names that were read from the page
Math that does not add up

questions.correct_answer: Math that does not add up
questions.intro: Look for four warning signs in an answer about a document. (1) MATH THAT DOES NOT ADD UP: items that do not sum to the stated total. (2) GARBLED WORDS: "Tota1 Arnount" instead of "Total Amount." (3) MISSING PARTS: no mention of a section you can see. (4) MIXED-UP ORDER: sentences from two columns stitched together. Any one sign means you should check the original. Example: items 12 + 8 + 5 with a stated total of 30 fail sign 1, because 12 + 8 + 5 = 25.

sections.title: Apply it

questions.domain: Everyday: searching and working with documents
questions.prompt: What question helps reveal how much of a file a tool read?

choices.text: "Are you confident that your answer about the whole file is correct and complete?"

questions.correct_answer: "How many pages did you read?"
questions.intro: Some failures are silent. A tool might read only the first part of a long file, skip pages that are images, or treat a two-column layout as one jumbled column, mixing sentences together. Ask the tool what it can see, for example "How many pages did you read?" or "List the section headings you found," and compare with the document. For anything that matters, confirm important values against the original rather than the tool's reading of it.
